advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make issue teardown run before project teardown (e.g. delete tracked issues inside the jira_dc_project finalizer prior to deleting the project, or tolerate a 404 from an already-cascade-deleted issue as success).
evidence: conftest.py:189 `def jira_dc_project(track_issue: Callable[[str], None]) -> Iterator[str]:` — declaring track_issue as a dependency makes pytest set it up first and therefore tear it down LAST (reverse order), so the project finalizer runs first
conftest.py:217-219 project teardown: `DELETE /rest/api/2/project/{key}` then `_poll_until_404(.../project/{key})` runs before the issue teardown
conftest.py:182-185 `for key in keys: status, body = _request(f"/rest/api/2/issue/{key}", method="DELETE"); assert status in (204, 200)` — a cascade-deleted issue returns 404 here, failing the assert
conftest.py:192-194 docstring claims issues are 'deleted (and confirmed gone) before the project itself is deleted', which is the OPPOSITE of the actual pytest teardown order
test_harness_smoke.py:145-168 the only consumer creates the issue UNDER jira_dc_project and registers it with track_issue, so the cascade path is exercised
advisory.finding: Fixture teardown ordering is inverted relative to the documented contract: `jira_dc_project` depends on `track_issue`, so pytest tears down the project finalizer BEFORE the issue finalizer. Deleting the scratch project cascade-deletes its issues, after which `track_issue`'s teardown DELETEs an already-gone issue and hits `assert status in (204, 200)` on a 404, failing teardown.
scenarios: The round-trip smoke test runs on a native amd64 CI runner where Jira answers REST; teardown deletes the project first, cascade-removes the issue, then the issue finalizer 404s and raises.
advisory.suggested_fix: In track_issue's teardown, treat 404 as an acceptable terminal status (`assert status in (204, 200, 404)`) since the issue may already be gone via project cascade; or restructure so the project fixture deletes its issues before deleting itself.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit `timeout-minutes` to the `jira-dc-harness` job (e.g. 40–60) so a hung boot fails within a bounded budget rather than the 360-minute default.
evidence: `jira-dc-harness:` ... `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` with no `timeout-minutes` (external-integration.yml:263-270)
reconcile-bridge.yml:68 `timeout-minutes: 60`
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:59 `timeout-minutes: 10`
Ticket c97f comment: run 3 `ran 55 MINUTES ... never reached 'Starting the JIRA Plugin System'` — evidence a stuck boot can run indefinitely
advisory.finding: The new `jira-dc-harness` CI job sets no `timeout-minutes`, so a hung build or boot falls back to GitHub's default 360-minute job budget. The ticket's own evidence records boots that never became usable within an hour (Cargo watchdog kill at ~25min; a 55-minute run that never reached plugin startup), and other jobs in this repo cap runtime explicitly (reconcile-bridge.yml:68 `timeout-minutes: 60`, reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:59 `timeout-minutes: 10`).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `timeout-minutes: 40` under the `jira-dc-harness:` job alongside `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the readiness wait detect a crashed/exited container (e.g. `docker compose ps`/exit-status check) and fail fast instead of polling the full budget.
evidence: external-integration.yml:297-302: `for i in $(seq 1 240); do if curl -fsS http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/api/2/serverInfo ...; then ... break; fi; sleep 5; done` — no `docker compose ps`/exit-code check
Ticket c97f comment: `the container ran ~25 minutes and then EXITED 1` — a crash inside container startup the readiness probe cannot detect
external-integration.yml:297 `for i in $(seq 1 240)` with `sleep 5` => ~1200s = 20 min budget
Dockerfile:62 `ENTRYPOINT ["atlas-run", ..., "-Dproduct.start.timeout=2700000"]` (45 min)
docker-compose.yml:40-43: on a cold cache `atlas-run` re-downloads ~917 artifacts, so first-start readiness is dominated by that download
advisory.finding: The 'Wait for Jira DC to become ready' step only polls the REST endpoint and never checks whether the container is still running. If `docker compose up` succeeded but the container exited (the exact failure mode the ticket documents: `DeployerWatchdog ... failed to finish deploying within the timeout period [600000]` -> container exits), the loop cannot short-circuit and burns the full 240×5s (~20 min) before reporting failure.
merged_from: The CI readiness wait budget (240×5s = 20 min) is shorter than the container's own boot ceiling `-Dproduct.start.timeout=2700000` (45 min). A slow-but-eventually-successful boot (cold Maven cache re-downloading ~917 artifacts, contended runner) can be aborted by the wait step at 20 min even though the container has not yet given up, producing a false failure.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/enforce integrity verification (checksums) for the runtime-downloaded Maven artifacts, or explicitly accept the unpinned-Jira risk in the provenance notes.
evidence: Dockerfile: 'this image does NOT contain Jira. `atlas-run` downloads Jira ${JIRA_VERSION} (~917 artifacts) from maven.atlassian.com on first container start'
README: 'Pinning this Dockerfile's base digest does NOT pin Jira itself.'
docker-compose.yml mounts a Maven cache but no artifact checksum verification is configured
`FROM addono/jira-software-standalone@sha256:04326628dc4ac36b2bfc1d0f2ebe5ba3807c1ec9cf9b18307d3c2ad7222537e9`
README 'What this is': 'Base image: `addono/jira-software-standalone`, pinned by digest' — publisher trust is not discussed
advisory.finding: Jira 8.17.1 and its ~917 Maven artifacts are downloaded at container-start time from maven.atlassian.com with no integrity verification (checksum/digest), so the actual software under test is an unpinned, unverified runtime supply-chain input despite the base image being digest-pinned.
merged_from: The base image `addono/jira-software-standalone` is a third-party community Docker Hub image (not an official Atlassian image) pinned by digest, with no documented provenance/trust rationale for the publisher.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin third-party GitHub Actions (`actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-python`) to immutable commit SHAs, matching repo convention if one exists.
evidence: `- uses: actions/checkout@v7`
`- uses: actions/setup-python@v6`
advisory.finding: Third-party GitHub Actions in the new jira-dc-harness job are pinned to mutable major-version tags (`actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-python@v6`) rather than immutable commit SHAs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the upstream license of the vendored pycontribs/jira Dockerfile (SPDX id / link) alongside the attribution.
evidence: Dockerfile header: 'this file is a vendored reproduction of that upstream Dockerfile (attribution: pycontribs/jira, docker/jira-test-image/Dockerfile)'
README 'Licensing' section: 'No licensing claim is made here.' — addresses the Jira instance license, not the vendored Dockerfile's upstream license
advisory.finding: The vendored Dockerfile reproduces pycontribs/jira's `docker/jira-test-image/Dockerfile` with prose attribution but no accompanying upstream license/NOTICE reference, leaving the license posture of the vendored artifact undocumented.
